main.title: Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
main.summary: Excavators led by Howard Carter began opening Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings on 4 November 1922.

cards.heading: Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
cards.text: Excavators led by Howard Carter began opening Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings on 4 November 1922. Debris had concealed the burial for centuries, protecting most of its contents from robbery. More than five thousand objects survived, many so fragile that their removal demanded extensive conservation. News of the discovery spread worldwide and inspired Egyptian designs in Western fashion and decoration. In Egypt, recently granted partial independence from Britain, the near-intact royal burial also became a source of national pride and tension with the British-led excavation.

main.title: Einstein: the 1921 Nobel Prize, awarded in 1922
main.subtitle: Light in discrete packets
main.summary: Einstein received the reserved 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922, especially for his explanation of the photoelectric effect.

cards.heading: Light in discrete packets
cards.text: Albert Einstein received the reserved 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922. The award especially recognised his law of the photoelectric effect. His 1905 explanation described light transferring energy in discrete packets: increasing its frequency can release electrons from a material even when making lower-frequency light brighter cannot. The work contributed to the emerging quantum description of nature. Einstein was travelling in Asia during the Stockholm ceremony in December 1922.

main.title: The Walt Disney Company
main.summary: Walt and Roy Disney founded the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio on 16 October 1923.

cards.heading: The Walt Disney Company
cards.text: Walt and Roy Disney founded the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio on 16 October 1923. Their animation business gained a defining success with Steamboat Willie in 1928, whose synchronised sound helped popularise Mickey Mouse. The character became the company's mascot as the studio grew. Disney later expanded into live-action films, television and theme parks during the 1950s. Those activities turned a small animation studio into a wider entertainment company, while its animated characters remained the most familiar connection between its different forms of storytelling.

main.title: The first 24 Hours of Le Mans
main.subtitle: Speed tested against time and reliability
main.summary: The first 24 Hours of Le Mans took place on 26–27 May 1923, testing the endurance of touring cars.

cards.heading: Speed tested against time and reliability
cards.text: The first 24 Hours of Le Mans began on May 26, 1923, and ended the following day. Georges Durand, Charles Faroux and Émile Coquille conceived a test in which touring cars had to run through an entire day and night, making reliability and teamwork as important as speed. Thirty-three cars started on the roads around Le Mans. André Lagache and René Léonard shared the number 9 Chenard & Walcker, completing 128 laps and more than 2,200 kilometres to lead the inaugural result.

main.title: The Great Gatsby
main.summary: F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1925 novel follows Nick Carraway and the millionaire Jay Gatsby in Jazz Age Long Island.

cards.heading: The Great Gatsby
cards.text:
The Great Gatsby is a 1925 tragedy novel by American writer F. Scott Fitzgerald. Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, near New York City, the novel depicts first-person narrator Nick Carraway's interactions with Jay Gatsby, a mysterious millionaire obsessed with reuniting with his former lover, Daisy Buchanan.

The novel was inspired by a youthful romance Fitzgerald had with socialite Ginevra King and the riotous parties he attended on Long Island's North Shore in 1922. Following a move to the French Riviera, Fitzgerald completed a rough draft of the novel in 1924. He submitted it to editor Maxwell Perkins, who persuaded Fitzgerald to revise the work over the following winter. After making revisions, Fitzgerald was satisfied with the text but remained ambivalent about the book's title and considered several alternatives. Painter Francis Cugat's dust jacket art, named Celestial Eyes, greatly impressed Fitzgerald, and he incorporated its imagery into the novel.

main.title: John Logie Baird: a television demonstration
main.summary: On 26 January 1926, John Logie Baird demonstrated his television system to members of the Royal Institution in his London laboratory.

cards.heading: John Logie Baird: a television demonstration
cards.text: On 26 January 1926, John Logie Baird demonstrated his mechanical television system to members of the Royal Institution in his London laboratory. The Scottish inventor's work helped bring moving images from an experimental apparatus towards home entertainment. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission. His later work included publicly demonstrated colour television and an electronic colour picture tube, extending the experiments that had brought the 1926 demonstration to public attention.

main.title: Metropolis
main.summary: Fritz Lang's Metropolis brought a vast futuristic city to the silent screen in 1927.

cards.heading: Metropolis
cards.text: Fritz Lang's Metropolis brought a vast futuristic city to the silent screen in 1927. Written with Thea von Harbou from her novel, the film follows Freder, the city master's son, and Maria as they try to bridge the divide between rulers and workers. Its urban dystopia made class conflict the centre of an ambitious science-fiction spectacle. Production at Babelsberg took seventeen months during 1925–1926 and cost more than five million Reichsmarks. The finished film became a pioneering feature-length work of science-fiction cinema.

main.title: Spirit of St. Louis
main.summary: Charles Lindbergh completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in Spirit of St. Louis on 20–21 May 1927.

cards.heading: Spirit of St. Louis
cards.text: Charles Lindbergh flew Spirit of St. Louis from New York to Paris on 20–21 May 1927, completing the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight. The purpose-built Ryan monoplane had one engine and one seat. Leaving Roosevelt Airfield on Long Island, Lindbergh reached Le Bourget after 33 hours and 30 minutes, covering about 5,800 kilometres and winning the $25,000 Orteig Prize. Ryan Airlines built the aircraft in San Diego. It later entered the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum, preserving the machine behind the celebrated crossing.

main.title: The Jazz Singer
main.summary: The Jazz Singer arrived in 1927 with synchronised recorded music, singing and passages of speech, helping turn sound films into a commercial force.

cards.heading: The Jazz Singer
cards.text: The Jazz Singer arrived in 1927 with synchronised recorded music, singing and passages of speech, helping turn sound films into a commercial force. Alan Crosland directed the Warner Bros. production using the Vitaphone sound-on-disc system. Al Jolson plays Jakie Rabinowitz, who leaves his devout Jewish family to become the entertainer Jack Robin. His ambitions collide with his father's expectations and his religious heritage. Six songs and several spoken sequences sit within a partly silent film, capturing a moment when cinema's familiar form was changing.

main.title: Fleming discovers penicillin
main.summary: Alexander Fleming discovered the antibacterial effect of Penicillium mould in 1928 at St Mary's Hospital in London. The observation began the development of penicillin into a medicine that transformed the treatment of bacterial infections.

cards.heading: Fleming discovers penicillin
cards.text:
Alexander Fleming discovered the antibacterial effect of Penicillium mould in 1928 at St Mary's Hospital in London. The observation began the development of penicillin into a medicine that transformed the treatment of bacterial infections.

Penicillins are antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds. They were among the earliest effective medicines against many infections caused by staphylococci and streptococci, changing the treatment of bacterial disease. Production developed through fermentation, followed by purification of the compounds. Their widespread use also brought the problem of bacterial resistance, making the history of penicillin a history of both medical advances and changing responses from the organisms it was used against.
